candidates.title: Task Order Drives Self-Improving Agent Performance Variance
candidates.scientific_question: Does task execution order alter self-improving agent performance variance?
candidates.observed_trigger: Shuffled task orders create 4.4% best-worst performance gap in WebArena GitLab subset
candidates.strongest_same_information_baseline: Fixed-order task execution with matched RBank memory
candidates.baseline_counterexample: Shuffled runs have 1.98% std dev vs fixed-order lower variance
candidates.closest_known_explanation: Memory underspecification from shuffled task sequences
candidates.residual_after_reduction: Unaccounted variance from order-induced memory issues
candidates.paper_level_claim: Task order is a critical source of performance variance in self-improving agents

adversarial_triage.provisional_basin_signature: Task ordering effects on self-improving agent performance variance.
adversarial_triage.strongest_same_information_attack: Shuffled vs fixed order variance may be due to insufficient runs; no confidence intervals for 4.4% gap.
adversarial_triage.possible_direct_counterevidence: No direct counterevidence; fixed-order lower variance could be sampling artifact.
adversarial_triage.cheapest_decisive_falsifier: WebArena GitLab subset, fixed vs shuffled order, performance std dev; stop if gap >2%.
adversarial_triage.support_blocker: Missing significance test; no control for memory contamination from previous runs.
adversarial_triage.duplicate_or_collision_target: None among candidates; may overlap with curriculum learning basin.
adversarial_triage.what_must_be_true_for_paper: Task order is sole cause of performance variance, not agent stochasticity.

candidates.title: Cumulative Skill Memory Accumulation Degrades Agent Performance
candidates.scientific_question: Does unpruned skill memory accumulation harm retrieval quality?
candidates.observed_trigger: Disabling pruning (ρ=0) lets low-utility skills accumulate, reducing SR
candidates.structural_variable: Cumulative skill memory entries over episodes
candidates.baseline_counterexample: ρ=0 runs have lower SR than optimally pruned settings

cheapest_falsifier.intervention_or_comparison: ρ=0 vs ρ=0.4 vs optimal τ=0.2

candidates.closest_known_explanation: Low-utility skill clutter reduces retrieval precision
candidates.residual_after_reduction: Unquantified impact of pruning threshold on memory utility
candidates.paper_level_claim: Skill memory pruning avoids degradation from accumulation

adversarial_triage.provisional_basin_signature: Skill memory pruning and retrieval quality in agents.
adversarial_triage.strongest_same_information_attack: SR drop without pruning could be due to retrieval noise; optimal pruning already known.
adversarial_triage.possible_direct_counterevidence: No direct counterevidence; pruning thresholds are well-studied.
adversarial_triage.cheapest_decisive_falsifier: xBench, ρ=0 vs ρ=0.4 vs τ=0.2, measure SR; stop if gap >3%.
adversarial_triage.support_blocker: No ablation across multiple pruning thresholds; effect may not be from accumulation.
adversarial_triage.duplicate_or_collision_target: None among candidates; may overlap with MEM-SEAR basin.
adversarial_triage.what_must_be_true_for_paper: Low-utility skills degrade retrieval, not just increase retrieval time.

candidates.title: Evolving Memory Reduces Task Forgetting in Continual Learning Agents
candidates.scientific_question: Does persistent memory evolution reduce task forgetting?
candidates.observed_trigger: Removing memory updates increases forgetting to 0.83
candidates.baseline_counterexample: Full HCL has higher final performance and lower forgetting
candidates.closest_known_explanation: Anchored memory retains successful/failed case histories
candidates.residual_after_reduction: Unmodeled retention benefits of anchor-based memory
candidates.paper_level_claim: Memory evolution reduces forgetting in continual learning

adversarial_triage.provisional_basin_signature: Memory evolution in continual learning for reduced forgetting.
adversarial_triage.strongest_same_information_attack: Forgetting reduction may be from replay of memory, not evolution; no fixed replay baseline.
adversarial_triage.possible_direct_counterevidence: Standard replay methods without memory updates achieve low forgetting; HCL may not be superior.
adversarial_triage.cheapest_decisive_falsifier: HCL setup, enable vs disable memory updates, measure forgetting; stop if >0.7.
adversarial_triage.support_blocker: No comparison to simple replay baselines; forgetting rate 0.83 might be an upper bound.
adversarial_triage.duplicate_or_collision_target: Overlap with MEM-OPEN-29a589216cf210fa68 and continual learning basins.
adversarial_triage.what_must_be_true_for_paper: Memory updates capture unique failure cases beyond replay, reducing forgetting.

candidates.title: Failure-derived memory drives persistent self-evolving agent failures
candidates.scientific_question: Do failure-derived memory retrievals cause persistent agent failures via reward inflation?
candidates.observed_trigger: All 10 persistent failures linked to failure-derived memory retrievals (0.647 ASR)
candidates.strongest_same_information_baseline: Success-derived retrievals (0.931 ASR, no persistent failures)
candidates.baseline_counterexample: Failure-derived retrievals have far lower ASR and all persistent failures
candidates.closest_known_explanation: Memory reward inflation from stored self-grade annotations
candidates.residual_after_reduction: Why only failure-derived retrievals trigger all persistent failures
candidates.paper_level_claim: Failure-derived memory retrievals are a causal driver of persistent agent failures

adversarial_triage.provisional_basin_signature: Memory-driven failure persistence in self-evolving agents.
adversarial_triage.strongest_same_information_attack: Failure-derived retrievals may involve harder tasks, causing lower ASR and persistent failures, not memory source.
adversarial_triage.possible_direct_counterevidence: If task difficulty matched, failure-derived retrievals might show ASR similar to success-derived.
adversarial_triage.cheapest_decisive_falsifier: Swap failure/success memory labels; if ASR gap closes, memory source isn't causal.
adversarial_triage.support_blocker: Label-swapping experiment not done; causal direction unconfirmed.
adversarial_triage.what_must_be_true_for_paper: Failure-derived memory retrievals, not task difficulty, cause lower ASR and persistent failures.

candidates.title: Underspecified memory causes amplified run variance in self-improving agents
candidates.scientific_question: Does underspecified memory explain amplified run variance with shuffled tasks?
candidates.observed_trigger: 4.4% best/worst gap, 1.98% std dev in GitLab WebArena subset
candidates.strongest_same_information_baseline: Runs using ground-truth reward for memory construction
candidates.baseline_counterexample: Proxy reward runs have higher run variance

cheapest_falsifier.intervention_or_comparison: Add proxy reward noise to memory

candidates.closest_known_explanation: Manual inspection linked underspecification to variance
candidates.residual_after_reduction: Why shuffled task orders amplify this variance specifically
candidates.paper_level_claim: Underspecified memory from proxy rewards causes run variance

adversarial_triage.provisional_basin_signature: Memory underspecification and run variance in self-improving agents.
adversarial_triage.strongest_same_information_attack: Proxy reward noise directly causes variance, not memory underspecification. Shuffled tasks amplify noise, not memory effects.
adversarial_triage.possible_direct_counterevidence: If ground-truth memory runs also show high variance under shuffled tasks, proxy reward is not the cause.
adversarial_triage.cheapest_decisive_falsifier: Add proxy reward noise to ground-truth memory; if run variance doesn't match proxy memory runs, claim is false.
adversarial_triage.support_blocker: No experiment isolating memory underspecification from proxy noise; causal link unconfirmed.
adversarial_triage.what_must_be_true_for_paper: Proxy reward noise causes memory underspecification, which then causes run variance, not other factors.

candidates.title: Recurring temporal grounding failures across agent tiers in time series tasks
candidates.scientific_question: Why do agents fail consistently at temporal grounding in evolving time series?
candidates.observed_trigger: Recurring temporal validity, exogenous context failures across model tiers
candidates.strongest_same_information_baseline: GPT-5.4/Qwen-3.5-397B (top overall but still has gaps)
candidates.baseline_counterexample: All models score <90% on hard time series tasks

cheapest_falsifier.setup: Reuse WASDE Crop Balance scenario runs

candidates.closest_known_explanation: Capability gap in forward-looking temporal analysis
candidates.residual_after_reduction: Why high-cost Sonnet-4.6 does not lead in accuracy
candidates.paper_level_claim: Temporal grounding failures recur across agent tiers in evolving time series

adversarial_triage.provisional_basin_signature: Temporal grounding failures in agent-based time series tasks.
adversarial_triage.strongest_same_information_attack: Temporal grounding failures stem from missing exogenous context, not agent capability. Models lack data, not reasoning.
adversarial_triage.possible_direct_counterevidence: If explicit temporal prompts fail to improve accuracy, temporal grounding is not the root cause.
adversarial_triage.cheapest_decisive_falsifier: Add explicit temporal grounding prompts; if scores don't improve >5%, temporal grounding is not the failure cause.
adversarial_triage.support_blocker: No direct manipulation of temporal grounding; correlation may not be causation.
adversarial_triage.what_must_be_true_for_paper: Temporal grounding is the specific missing ability, not other factors like data access or integration.

candidates.title: Failure-derived memory retrievals cause persistent agent failures
candidates.scientific_question: Do failure-derived memory retrievals directly cause persistent agent skill failures?
candidates.observed_trigger: 34 failure retrievals had 0.647 accuracy +10 persistent failures, vs 0.931 for success retrievals
candidates.structural_variable: Type of memory retrieved (failure vs success-derived)
candidates.strongest_same_information_baseline: Success-derived memory retrieval (0.931 accuracy, no failures)
candidates.baseline_counterexample: Failure-derived retrievals produce 0.647 accuracy +10 persistent failures
candidates.closest_known_explanation: Memory reward inflation or underspecified content
candidates.residual_after_reduction: Why failure-specific retrievals uniquely drive persistent failures?
candidates.paper_level_claim: Failure-derived memory retrievals causal for persistent self-evolving agent failures

adversarial_triage.provisional_basin_signature: Failure-derived memory retrieval causes persistent agent skill failures.
adversarial_triage.strongest_same_information_attack: Success-derived retrieval already reaches 0.931 accuracy, zero failures; effect may be due to content quality, not retrieval type.
adversarial_triage.possible_direct_counterevidence: None; no direct counterevidence in provided refs.
adversarial_triage.cheapest_decisive_falsifier: Swap failure/success retrieval labels; if group gaps close, causality is refuted. Low effort, <10h.
adversarial_triage.support_blocker: No mechanism for why failure retrievals uniquely cause persistent failures, not just lower accuracy.
adversarial_triage.what_must_be_true_for_paper: Failure-derived retrievals must contain unique failure-causing information beyond content quality or reward.

candidates.title: Noisy proxy rewards increase self-improving agent run variance
candidates.scientific_question: Does noisy proxy reward memory cause run-to-run variance?
candidates.observed_trigger: 4.4% best/worst gap, 1.98% std dev in GitLab WebArena subset
candidates.structural_variable: Memory reward signal type (ground-truth vs proxy)
candidates.baseline_counterexample: Proxy reward use correlates with higher run variance
candidates.closest_known_explanation: Underspecified memory from noisy proxy signals
candidates.residual_after_reduction: Why task order shuffling amplifies this variance?
candidates.paper_level_claim: Noisy proxy reward memory increases self-improving agent run variance

adversarial_triage.provisional_basin_signature: Noisy proxy reward signals increase run-to-run variance in self-improving agents.
adversarial_triage.strongest_same_information_attack: Ground-truth reward runs already show lower variance; proxy noise may be confounded with other run differences.
adversarial_triage.cheapest_decisive_falsifier: Remove proxy reward noise in GitLab subset; if variance drops >50%, noise is causal. Low effort.
adversarial_triage.support_blocker: Unclear if task order shuffling rather than proxy noise drives variance amplification.
adversarial_triage.what_must_be_true_for_paper: Proxy reward noise must be the primary driver of increased variance, independent of other run factors.

candidates.title: Missing temporal skills cause time series agent failures
candidates.scientific_question: Do missing temporal/exogenous context skills cause recurring failures?
candidates.observed_trigger: Agents over-commit to single commodity, high-cost models underperform on hard tasks
candidates.baseline_counterexample: Hard tier tasks show wider model performance gaps
candidates.closest_known_explanation: Lack of specialized analytical skills for temporal tasks
candidates.residual_after_reduction: Why high-cost models still fail at these tasks?
candidates.paper_level_claim: Missing temporal/exogenous skills cause time series agent failures

adversarial_triage.provisional_basin_signature: Missing temporal/exogenous skills cause time series agent failures.
adversarial_triage.strongest_same_information_attack: Strong models on easy tasks lack temporal skills but still fail on hard tasks; task complexity alone may explain gap.
adversarial_triage.cheapest_decisive_falsifier: Add temporal skills to TimeSage-1.0; if over-commitment drops, skills are causal. Medium effort.
adversarial_triage.support_blocker: High-cost models failing on hard tasks may be due to insufficient domain adaptation, not just missing temporal skills.
adversarial_triage.what_must_be_true_for_paper: Temporal/exogenous skills are necessary and sufficient to reduce over-commitment and failures on hard tasks.
